messages:
liz_support: FYI ACME Prod -> internal-api.acme.svc is returning NXDOMAIN for our Private deployment in us-east-1, customer reports app-level 401s downstream. They're escalating to security. Can SRE/netops triage?

acme_prod_owner: Confirmed. Started seeing 401s ~09:15 UTC. curl to our Redwood endpoint returns 401 because the app cannot reach internal API (DNS failure). Repro steps in case useful: 
1) inside prod bastion: `dig internal-api.acme.svc @10.0.0.2 +short` -> nothing
2) from app pod: `nslookup internal-api.acme.svc` -> server can't find internal-api.acme.svc: NXDOMAIN

liz_support: Thanks — adding details from the customer: they ran a Route53 hosted zone migration yesterday (moved some private hosted zones between accounts). They think there might be an overlap or mis-assoc between the new hosted zone and the prod VPC.

oncall_bot: Route53 change detected: hosted-zone ZH123EXAMPLE moved at 1767889000 by carla_netops (reason: hosted-zone split/owner transfer).

ben_sre: Oof. Likely split-view: two private hosted zones with same name but different VPC associations, or hosted zone not associated to the prod VPC. First checks: (a) which HostedZoneId is answering the VPC resolver and (b) VPC association list. Can someone paste `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id <id>` for the zone name?

carla_netops: Pulled the associations quickly — looks like the new private hosted zone (ZH123EXAMPLE) is ONLY associated to staging VPCs. Prod VPC (vpc-0a1b2c3d) is NOT in the VPCs list. CLI snippet: 

```
$ aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id ZH123EXAMPLE
{
  "HostedZone": {
    "Id": "/hostedzone/ZH123EXAMPLE",
    "Name": "acme.svc.",
    "Config": {
      "PrivateZone": true,
      "Comment": "migrated private zone"
    },
    "VPCs": [
      { "VPCRegion": "us-east-1", "VPCId": "vpc-0f1e2d3c" }  # staging only
    ]
  }
}
```

ben_sre: That matches NXDOMAIN from prod resolver — prod VPC isn't associated so it won't see that private zone. We used to have a zone with same name in the old account; if that old zone was deleted, resolver returns NXDOMAIN. Two mitigation paths: associate the correct hosted zone to prod VPC (if ownership is correct) or add a VPC resolver rule/forwarder to route queries to the account with the zone. Which is the intended ownership? @carla_netops

carla_netops: ACME's intent was to centralize private zones in account A (staging) then share via VPC associations to prod. During migration I missed adding the prod VPC association because of a permission error that I resolved later — I thought I added it post-change but looks like not. I'll create the association now. Will need a 1–2 minute maintenance on the route53 side; no infra deploys.

acme_prod_owner: Please hurry, their customer-facing feature is degraded. Any chance of a quick rollback to previous zone owner?

ben_sre: Rollback isn't possible if the old hosted zone was deleted. Best fast path is to associate the hosted zone to prod VPC. Carla — when you run `associate-vpc` we need to ensure: 
- call from owning account (account A)
- VPC region match
- route53:AssociateVPCWithHostedZone API returns "ChangeInfo"; watch for propagation.

carla_netops: Running it now: 
```
aws route53 associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone --hosted-zone-id ZH123EXAMPLE --vpc VPCRegion=us-east-1,VPCId=vpc-0a1b2c3d
```
Response: change submitted ID: /change/C123EXAMPLE (status PENDING)

ben_sre: After association, confirm with dig to the VPC resolver: `dig internal-api.acme.svc @10.0.0.2 +short` and also check node-local cache if applicable (curl from pod may be using nodelocaldns) — sometimes the nodelocal cache returns stale NXDOMAIN for a short period. If so, TTL purge or restart nodelocald can help.

liz_support: Noted — I'll tell the customer we are associating the zone and propagation may take a few minutes.

oncall_bot: Route53 Change C123EXAMPLE status: INSYNC at 1767890800

ben_sre: Verified from prod bastion at 1767890820: `dig internal-api.acme.svc @10.0.0.2 +short` -> `10.10.20.33` (resolution restored). Also ran `kubectl exec` into app pod: `nslookup internal-api.acme.svc` -> now returns the A record.

acme_prod_owner: Confirmed app recovered, 401s stopped. Customer seeing healthy now. Thanks team! :tada:

liz_support: Closing the escalation once ACME confirms. Action items: 
- carla_netops: follow-up to add prod VPC association to IaC and add guardrail so migrations must include VPC association step.
- ben_sre: add a runbook note for nodelocaldns cache purge after Route53 association changes.

carla_netops: Will open an infra PR and permission tweak ticket.

liz_support: Great job. Logging this thread for postmortem if ACME requests one.

ben_sre: Also flagging for the incident board: impact was customer-facing for ~45m, root cause: missing VPC association after hosted-zone migration.

acme_prod_owner: Appreciate the quick fix. Please share the postmortem when available.
